Riesling: High acid, low alcohol, dry to sweet: the fire code and the pork lover. Mosel for feather, Alsace for muscle.
Pinot Noir: Silk, cherry, forest floor: the red that crosses to fish and worships duck. Burgundy is the reference.
Cabernet: Cassis and structure: tannin built for seared beef and lamb; never near chile or delicate fish.
Malbec: Argentina’s velvet power: grilled beef’s constitutional partner; violets over char.
Syrah: Black pepper, olive, smoked meat: the braise and barbecue intellectual; Rhône savor.
Chardonnay: Chablis steel to Meursault cream: match the oak level to the butter level.
Sauvignon Blanc: Grass, gooseberry, cut lime, the vegetable and goat-cheese whisperer.
Albariño: Sea-spray salinity and white peach, shellfish’s Atlantic soulmate.
Chianti: Sour cherry and tomato-leaf acid: pasta, pizza, and bistecca by regional law.
Barbera: Chianti’s juicier cousin: high acid, low tannin, weeknight Italian everything.
Champagne: Acid plus bubbles: scrubs salt, fat, and fry; the universal rescue and the oyster’s crown.
Muscadet: Bone-dry, saline, lees-creamy: the oyster wine, priced like a secret.
Chablis: Unoaked Chardonnay on old seabeds, oyster shell in a glass.
Gewürztraminer: Lychee and rose, off-dry: aromatic armor for spice and coconut curries.
Sake: Amino-rich and gentle: umami’s bridge to dashi, soy, and sashimi.
Lager: Cold, clean, carbonated: fire’s honest antidote and fried food’s friend.
Stout: Roast and cream: oysters’ old flame and chocolate’s dark mirror.
Saison: Farmhouse spice and dry finish: charcuterie, pork, and picnic tables.
Fino sherry: Bone-dry, saline, almond: tapas, consommé, and anything from the sea.
Port: Fortified depth: blue cheese and chocolate’s appointed hour.
Sauternes: Botrytis honey and acid: foie, blue cheese, and custard desserts.
Rosé: Provence’s dry pink: the apéritif hour and the fried-food alliance.
Nebbiolo: Tar and roses, massive structure: truffles, braises, and mushroom depth; decant.
Tempranillo (Rioja): Cherry in American oak: vanilla and dill smoke-echo; lamb’s Spanish marriage.
Grenache/GSM: Strawberry, garrigue, warmth: Mediterranean plates and Middle-Eastern spice.
Gamay (Beaujolais): Chilled cherry joy: charcuterie, roast chicken, salmon; serve cool, always.
Chenin Blanc: Honey over screaming acid: pork with apples, gentle heat, cream sauces.
Vermentino: Coastal Italian herb-and-citrus: grilled fish and lighter tomato plates.
Grüner Veltliner: White pepper and lentil savor, the difficult-vegetable specialist and schnitzel’s law.
Assyrtiko: Santorini’s volcanic citrus-salt: whole grilled fish’s Greek answer.
Zinfandel: Bramble jam and pepper: American barbecue’s sweet-smoke handshake.
IPA: Hop bitterness and citrus: cuts fry and rich burgers; wrestles delicate food.
Witbier: Orange peel and coriander over wheat: mussels’ Belgian birthright.
Porter: Roast, chocolate, gentle smoke: braises, sausages, and smoked meats.
